grade.first_issue: The chosen Puiseux inverse branch is only local near infinity and need not attain every root of \(P\); therefore \(P(Q(x))=x^{2024}\) does not imply that \(P\) has only one distinct root.
grade.summary: The final classification is correct, and the coefficient analysis is largely sound once the pure-power form is assumed. However, the central argument establishing that form is invalid: a local inverse branch cannot control all roots of \(P\), and the further assertion that a Puiseux series with only one zero must be a monomial is also unjustified. A fundamentally different argument is needed.
strengths: Correctly excludes constant polynomials and states the complete correct family.
The divisibility, sign, and final verification arguments are essentially correct conditional on \(P(x)=a'(qx-p)^d\).

errors.description: The local Puiseux inverse \(Q\) need not take the value of each root of \(P\), so the deduction that \(P\) has only one distinct root is false.
Even knowing that \(Q(x)-r\) has only one zero would not justify the asserted identity \(Q(x)-r=c_rx^{m_r}\).
The use and global interpretation of Puiseux branches, including evaluation near \(x=0\), are not established.
